note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 52; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 22) on data/benches/calorimeter.json: the heat of neutralisation. q = m c dT (the solution's mass, about 4.18 J/(g K), the rise), over the moles of water made: about -56 kJ/mol, a little less in the cup, which loses some and holds some.
title: Experiment: the heat of neutralisation

steps.title: 50 mL of the base
steps.text: Pick up the sodium hydroxide, right-click the cylinder, type 50 and click "pour". Right-click the cylinder and write down what it reads.
steps.why: A 100 mL cylinder reads to a tenth of its 1 mL divisions, within 0.5 mL. You poured about 50: the cylinder says how much.

steps.title: Into the cup
steps.text: Pick up the cylinder, right-click the cup, drag the slider to the end and click "pour it all". Right-click the cup and write down its thermometer's reading: the start.
steps.why: The foam cup and its lid let little heat through: what the reaction gives out stays in the solution, nearly all of it.

steps.title: 25 mL of the acid
steps.text: Pick up the sulfuric acid, right-click the cylinder, type 25 and click "pour". Write down what the cylinder reads.
steps.why: 25 mL of 1 M sulfuric acid neutralises 50 mL of 1 M sodium hydroxide exactly: H2SO4 + 2 NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2 H2O, 0.050 mol of water made.

steps.title: The acid into the cup
steps.text: Pick up the cylinder, right-click the cup, drag the slider to the end and click "pour it all". Then right-click the cup and click "stir".

steps.title: The highest temperature
steps.text: Watch the thermometer climb, and write down the highest it reads.
steps.why: The thermometer follows the solution a few seconds behind (its probe's lag), and the cup slowly loses heat to the room: the highest reading is a little under the rise the reaction gave. A careful lab draws the cooling back to the moment of mixing. dH = -m c dT / n(water).

results.label: the water the reaction made (the truth: sodium sulfate in it, a mole for two of water)
